observations: A TV screen displays a PlayStation 4 dashboard with game tiles for Mortal Kombat 11 Ultimate, FC25, and WWE 2K24.
The game tiles show CUSA ID codes (e.g., CUSA11379), which are typical of jailbroken console interfaces.
A hand holds a clear plastic case containing two blue-surfaced Blu-ray discs.
A black PlayStation 4 Slim console is visible on a shelf below the TV.
The screen shows a user profile named 'User1'.
Watermarks for 'GMC GAME STUDIOS' and 'Gameready.ng | Lagos' are visible on the image.

claims.claim: jailbreak your PS4 with Blu-ray disc

risks.risk: The jailbreak exploit (likely PPPwn) only works on specific firmware versions (typically 11.00 or lower).
risks.proof: A video of the console's 'Settings > System > System Information' screen showing the System Software version.
risks.if_unproven: as a standard blank or burnt Blu-ray disc

risks.risk: The discs may be low-quality BD-R burns that are difficult for the console's laser to read or may degrade quickly.
risks.proof: A video showing the disc being inserted and successfully triggering the exploit menu on the console.

proof_requests: Video of the PS4 System Information screen showing the current firmware version.
Video demonstration of the disc successfully launching the jailbreak/GoldHEN menu.
Clear photos of the data side of the discs to check for scratches or burn quality.
response.reason: The item is identified as a PS4 jailbreak tool delivered via Blu-ray media. It can be priced at the value of a basic software modification service or burnt media, with the understanding that its utility is entirely dependent on the buyer's console firmware version.
